sources.entry: Agents Can Communicate (ACC) by Mykola Maksymenko - Local, multi-provider agent communication tool. Adds hooks and a skill to exchange questions and reviews, and saves decisions, verification results and handoffs for later sessions. Each session keeps its own client, model, conversation and permissions.

summary.one_liner: A local, multi-provider tool (npm package agents-can-communicate, CLI "acc") that lets separate coding-agent sessions such as Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI exchange questions, reviews and handoffs with each other.
summary.what_it_does: ACC installs hooks and a skill into supported coding clients so that sessions running on the same machine can message one another, including sessions the user opened themselves. Messages are delivered at the next turn for verified integrations, or other sessions read their ACC inbox explicitly. Sessions can ask questions, request reviews naming specific files, and check whether a question was delivered and answered. Decisions, verification results and handoffs are saved so a later session in a different client can pick up unfinished work without a transcript. Each session keeps its own model, conversation and permissions, and no lead agent coordinates the others. Coordination stays local, with messages and handoffs stored in local app data outside the project. An optional experimental live-delivery mode can wake eligible sessions, and it is off by default.
use_cases: Have Claude Code and Codex sessions coordinate on one feature in the same project
Get a second opinion on a change from a model in another client
Hand off unfinished work with decisions and next steps when switching clients
Ask another running agent session a question about a shared API
Track which agent session is working on which task to avoid conflicts
how_to_run: Follow the installer's activation instructions and review any required hook or plugin trust
Restart your clients from the project directory
Run acc doctor from the project if a peer is missing or delivery differs from expectations
notable: Lets sessions you opened yourself message each other across different clients, in either direction
Handoffs record decisions, unfinished work and verification results rather than full transcripts
Runs locally with no separate account, model API key or hosted service
Works natively on Windows 10/11 without WSL
Other clients can connect through MCP with their own configuration
caveats: Live delivery is experimental, requires opt-in and an active verified connection, and can spend model tokens
Requires supported coding clients installed on the same machine and operating-system user
Agents decide when to coordinate, and ACC does not guarantee they notice every dependency
